_about: Shared question bank. A question has one id across every region pack, so a learner answers once and each pack's tree uses the answer. Questions with fromProduct are answered from the product profile; they can still be flipped in what-if.

bio.text: Is the product a biological product licensed under a BLA?
bio.help: Biologics follow 21 CFR 601.12 and FDA's 2021 guidance for certain biological products, which treat many process changes more strictly than for small molecules.

anda.text: Is the application an ANDA (a generic)?
anda.help: ANDA holders report changes under 21 CFR 314.97, which applies 314.70; labeling must stay the same as the reference listed drug.

aseptic.text: Is the sterile product made by aseptic processing (not terminally sterilized)?
aseptic.help: Aseptic processing has less margin for error than terminal sterilization, so moves and equipment changes are classified more strictly.

mr.text: Is it a modified-release dosage form (extended or delayed release)?
mr.help: Changes that may affect controlled release are major changes in the US guidance.

solidOral.text: Is it a solid oral dosage form (tablet or capsule)?

doseControl.text: Does the primary packaging control the dose delivered to the patient (for example a metered-dose valve or an auto-injector)?

siteNeverInspected.text: Has the regulator (FDA in the US) never inspected the new site for this type of operation, or would the move restart an operation stopped there for more than two years?
siteNeverInspected.help: Either one makes a site move a prior approval supplement (guidance section VI.B.1).

siteCgmp.text: Does the new site have a satisfactory CGMP inspection for this type of operation?
siteCgmp.help: If the last inspection for this operation was not satisfactory, the move needs prior approval (VI.B.2).

asepticNewOrDissimilar.text: Is the aseptic facility or area newly built or refurbished, or does it not yet make similar approved products (same container types and sizes)?
asepticNewOrDissimilar.help: VI.B.4 sets prior approval for both cases; a move into an existing aseptic area that already makes similar approved products is a CBE-30 (VI.C.1.b).

termNewFacilityOtherSite.text: Is the product moving to a newly constructed facility at a different site?
termNewFacilityOtherSite.help: VI.B.5. A move to a new or existing building on the same site is an annual report item (VI.D.5).

sameSiteBuilding.text: Is the move to a new or existing building on the same manufacturing site?

bioAltLineApproved.text: Is the new filling line already approved for aseptic manufacture of other products, with no change to the validated process?
bioAltLineApproved.help: FDA's 2021 biologics guidance lists that case as a CBE-30; other fill-line additions that may affect sterility assurance need prior approval.

finalIntermediate.text: Is the material the final intermediate of the drug substance synthesis?
finalIntermediate.help: The final intermediate is the last compound before the reaction that forms the drug substance.

testingConditions.text: Will the new laboratory use the approved test procedures, are all commitments on those procedures fulfilled, and can it do the testing?
testingConditions.help: All three are conditions of VI.C.1.d.

componentSterilizationSame.text: Is the sterilization process for the packaging components materially the same as the approved one?

affectsSterility.text: Could the change affect sterility assurance (sterilization method, sterilizer load, aseptic equipment, lyophilizer, filter)?
affectsSterility.help: VII.B.2 makes these prior approval supplements.

fundamentalTech.text: Is it a fundamental change in process or technology (for example wet to dry granulation, or a new type of drying)?

affectsRelease.text: Could the change affect the controlled release, metering or other dose-delivery characteristics?

bioMinorParam.text: Is it only a minor change on the same equipment, within validated ranges, with no change in process parameters?
bioMinorParam.help: FDA's 2021 biologics guidance lists these as annual report changes; other process or scale changes for biologics usually need prior approval.

bulkHold50.text: Does the scale change increase bulk solution storage time by more than 50% beyond validated limits?
bulkHold50.help: Terminally sterilized products only: more than 50% is a CBE-30 (VII.C.1.d), up to 50% an annual report item (VII.D.6).

dsAfterFinalOrImpurity.text: Does the change affect steps after the final intermediate, or could it change the impurity profile of the drug substance?

inkApproved.text: Is the ink already used in products approved by CDER?
inkApproved.help: Yes: annual report (VII.D.3). No: prior approval (VII.B.6).

filterMaterialPore.text: Does the change involve the sterilizing filter material or pore size (not only filtration parameters such as flow, pressure or time)?

supacLevel.text: What SUPAC level is the composition change?

options.label: Level 1: deletion of a colour or flavour, or excipient changes within the Level 1 ranges (total additive effect up to 5%)
Level 2: excipient changes beyond Level 1 but within the Level 2 ranges (total up to 10%)
Level 3: changes beyond Level 2, a qualitative change, or a narrow therapeutic index drug beyond Level 1

supacLevel.help: From SUPAC-IR, which still governs components and composition. Modified-release and semisolid products have their own SUPAC tables; the app simplifies them to the same three levels.

compendial.text: Is the change made only to comply with an official pharmacopoeia (USP–NF, Ph. Eur.)?

rawMaterialPreFinal.text: Does it concern raw materials, starting materials or in-process materials used before the final intermediate in drug substance manufacture?

envMicro.text: Is it an in-process acceptance criterion for microbiological monitoring of the production environment, materials or components?
envMicro.help: Relaxing such a criterion is a CBE-30 (VIII.C.1.d).

adventitious.text: Does it concern testing raw materials for viruses or adventitious agents?
adventitious.help: Relaxing, deleting or weakening these tests needs prior approval (VIII.B.6).

sameOrBetter.text: Does the new or changed analytical procedure give the same or greater assurance than the approved one?

bioMethodMajor.text: Does the change alter the technique, the acceptance criteria or the method performance?
bioMethodMajor.help: For biologics, such changes (for example to a potency assay) need prior approval; minor modifications are annual report changes.

polymerNew.text: Is the new polymeric material (or ink or adhesive) new to approved products of the same dosage form and route?

sameOrBetterProtection.text: Does the new container closure give the same or better protection than the approved one?

appliesToDS.text: Is the container for the drug substance (not the drug product)?

unitOfUse.text: Is the product in a unit-of-use container?

blisterMaterialsApproved.text: Are the blister materials already used in approved products of the same type?

productContactChange.text: Does the change alter product-contact materials or the container dimensions?

approvedProtocolFullData.text: Is the extension based on full shelf-life data from production batches, under the stability protocol approved in the application?
approvedProtocolFullData.help: Yes: annual report (XI.C.1). An extension based on a new or revised protocol, or on accelerated or partial data, needs prior approval (XI.A.4).

stabilityTimepointsOnly.text: Is the change only adding time points, or deleting time points beyond the approved expiry date?

newlyAcquired.text: Is it based on newly acquired information with reasonable evidence of a causal association?
newlyAcquired.help: Under 21 CFR 314.70(c)(6)(iii) and 601.12(f)(2), safety labeling that adds or strengthens information on this basis may be put in place when FDA receives the supplement.

rldUpdate.text: Is the change only to match updated labeling of the reference listed drug?

cpCategory.text: Which reporting category did the approved comparability protocol set for this change?

options.label: Supplement - Changes Being Effected in 30 Days
Supplement - Changes Being Effected
Annual report

wcbApprovedProtocol.text: Is the new working cell bank made from the approved master cell bank under an approved qualification protocol?

bioResinMinor.text: Is it only a minor change to purification parameters (no new resin, step, column size or loading scale)?

editorialOnly.text: Is the change editorial only (no change in meaning or data)?

notBio.text: Is the product not a biological product?

irOral.text: Is it an immediate-release oral dosage form?

irFct.text: Is it an immediate-release film-coated tablet?

siteNeedsInspection.text: Does the new site need an initial or product-specific GMP inspection before it can be used?
siteNeedsInspection.help: In the EU this makes a site change Type II (Q.II.b.1(d)).

novelComplex.text: Is the finished product made by a novel or complex manufacturing process?
novelComplex.help: Q.II.b.1(c) and Q.II.b.4(d) make these Type II. The guidelines and EMA Q&A describe what counts; the app does not decide it for you.

asmfNew.text: Is the new active substance manufacturer supported by an Active Substance Master File (ASMF)?
asmfNew.help: A new ASMF-supported manufacturer is Type II (Q.I.a.1(f)).

significantDossierUpdate.text: Does the new site use a substantially different route or conditions, needing a significant update of the active substance part of the dossier?

bioProcedure.text: Is the analytical procedure biological, immunological or immunochemical?

lineDuplicate.text: Is the new line a duplicate of an approved line, with no change to the process?
lineDuplicate.help: For biologics, a scale change without process change (such as duplicating a line) is Type IB (Q.II.b.4(f)).

majorImpact.text: Could the change significantly affect the quality, safety or efficacy of the product?
majorImpact.help: Major changes are Type II. Use the guideline text and your risk assessment, not convenience.

comparabilityNeeded.text: Does the change need a comparability assessment (biologics) or a new bioequivalence study?

scaleWithin10.text: Is the new batch size within ten times the originally approved size (up or down)?

significantQuality.text: Could deleting it significantly affect the overall quality of the product?

excipientKind.text: What kind of excipient change is it?

options.label: A minor quantitative adjustment of excipients
Replacement with a comparable excipient with the same function
Another qualitative or quantitative change

colourAction.text: What happens to the colouring or flavouring component?

options.label: It is deleted (or added or replaced)
Its amount is increased or reduced

minorMethodChange.text: Is it a minor change to the approved procedure (same method type; for example column length or temperature)?

altAction.text: Is the alternative procedure being added (or revised), or deleted?

options.label: Added or revised
Deleted

containerTypeChange.text: Is it a change of container type, or a new container (for example vial to prefilled syringe, or bottle to blister)?

withinPackRange.text: Is the new pack size within the approved range of pack sizes?

piAffected.text: Does the change affect the product information (SmPC, labelling or package leaflet)?

realTimeData.text: Is the extension supported by real-time data in line with the approved stability protocol?

extrapolationPerGuideline.text: Is the extrapolation done in line with the relevant stability guidelines?

agencyOutcome.text: Does the change implement an outcome already assessed by the authorities (for example a PRAC signal, PSUSA or referral outcome)?

agreedExact.text: Is the wording exactly as agreed by the authorities, with agreed translations, needing no further assessment?

newData.text: Does the change need new data to be assessed?

pacmpType.text: Which category did the approved PACMP set for implementing this change?

options.label: Type IA
Type IA-IN
Type IB

refStdProtocol.text: Is the new reference standard qualified under a qualification protocol approved in the dossier?

refStdComparable.text: Are comparability results between the current and the new reference standard available?

nonStandardSterilisation.text: Is the new method a non-standard terminal sterilisation method (not a Ph. Eur. reference condition)?

sameGroup.text: Is the new manufacturer part of the same pharmaceutical group as the current one?
sameGroup.help: Under the 2013 guidelines this made a new active substance manufacturer Type IA-IN (B.I.a.1(a)).

existingSite.text: Is the new facility (or line) within an existing approved site?
existingSite.help: In India's biologics guidance a new geographic site is Level I; a new facility within an existing site is Level II.

seriousWarning.text: Is it a new contraindication or a serious new warning or precaution?
seriousWarning.help: In India's biologics guidance these are Level I; adding or strengthening other risk-management text is Level II.

centralised.text: Is the product authorised through the EU centralised procedure?

dsSameRoute.text: Does the new source use the same route of synthesis and meet the same drug substance specification, including impurity limits?
dsSameRoute.help: A different route or new impurities make the change a change to the drug substance process, which is classified more strictly.

cepCovers.text: Is the new source covered by a valid Ph. Eur. certificate of suitability (CEP)?
cepCovers.help: A CEP lets authorities rely on the EDQM assessment. Without one, the data come from a master file or the dossier.

releaseTesting.text: What will the new site do?

options.label: Batch release only (no testing)
Release and physicochemical or microbiological testing
Release and biological, immunological or immunochemical testing

scaleOnly.text: Is it only a change of scale, with equipment of the same design and operating principle and no change to the process or specifications?

ipcCritical.text: Does the in-process control cover a critical attribute, or could the change significantly affect quality?
ipcCritical.help: Critical attributes include assay, impurities, dissolution and sterility-related controls.

holdData.text: Is the longer hold time supported by data on batches held for the full proposed time, under an approved protocol?

dsScope.text: What does the design space change cover?

options.label: A new design space for a unit operation of the process
A new design space for an analytical procedure, excipient or intermediate
A change to, or extension of, an approved design space

isEC.text: In the approved dossier, is the element you are changing an established condition?
isEC.help: ICH Q12: only established conditions need a regulatory submission when they change. If no established conditions were agreed, treat the whole quality dossier as binding and classify the change in its own entry.

plcmCategory.text: Which reporting category does the approved PLCM document set for changing this established condition?

options.label: Prior approval
Notification, moderate (wait before implementing)
Notification, low (implement, then tell)

plcmCategory.help: ICH Q12 chapter 3 and Annex I: the PLCM lists each established condition with its reporting category.

options.label: A strength
A pack size

isReleaseSite.text: Is it the manufacturer responsible for batch release?

plcmMajor.text: Does the update raise risk, for example add or change established conditions or lower a reporting category?
plcmMajor.help: Lowering a reporting category or redefining established conditions needs assessment like a major change.

options.label: It is deleted
A minor change that does not change its strategy
A major change, for example new studies, acceptance criteria or scope

potencyNewPrinciple.text: Does the new potency assay use a different principle, for example a cell-based assay replacing a binding assay?

adventRisk.text: What do the new studies change?

options.label: Steps are tested for the first time for one or more agents
Obsolete studies are replaced and the risk is now higher
Obsolete studies are replaced and the risk is the same or lower

deviceSignificant.text: Could the device change significantly affect the dose delivered, quality, safety or efficacy?

scoredEqualDose.text: Is the tablet scored so that it can be divided into equal doses?

scoreAction.text: Is the score line added or deleted?

options.label: Added
Deleted

inUseKind.text: What is the change to the in-use period?

options.label: It becomes shorter
It becomes longer, based on real-time data
It becomes longer, based on extrapolation or modelling

restrictive.text: Are the new storage conditions more restrictive (for example a lower temperature)?

excipientSpecKind.text: What changes in the excipient specification?

options.label: A limit is tightened
A test is added
A non-significant test is deleted
A limit is widened or a significant test deleted

rmpKind.text: What kind of update is it?

options.label: It implements an outcome already assessed, with the exact agreed wording
A minor update (for example due dates or a template update)
It needs new data and a significant assessment

bioScaleOnly.text: Is it a scale change with no change to the process (for example adding identical bioreactors or duplicating a line)?

animalOrigin.text: Does the change introduce a material of human or animal origin that needs a viral safety or TSE assessment?

options.label: More cycles, under an approved resin lifetime protocol
A different resin or supplier

jpItem.text: How is the item you are changing described in the Japanese approval form?

options.label: As an approved matter (not marked as a minor change item)
As a minor change item
As a moderate change item (2024 trial)
As an annual report item (2025 trial)
It is not in the approval form

jpItem.help: In Japan the approval form (approved matters) is legally binding. The applicant proposes, and PMDA agrees, which entries are minor change items. Items not in the form are managed in the quality system.

pqInspected.text: Was the new site inspected and found compliant by WHO or a stringent regulatory authority within the last three years?
pqInspected.help: WHO PQ: a site without such an inspection makes a site addition a major variation.

caProtocolLevel.text: Which reporting level did the approved PACMP set for this change?

options.label: Level II notifiable change
Level III immediate notification
Level III annual notification

jpProtocolNotice.text: Is the change made fully as described in the approved PACMP, with all acceptance criteria met?

whoMinorU.text: Will you justify the change as an unclassified minor variation (suffix u), or have you agreed a lower category with PQT in advance?
whoMinorU.help: WHO PQ FAQ Q8: changes not listed in the guideline are major by default.
